title: JobSpec
description: One exp-runner job: a repo + a task + a natural-language acceptance description + an agent. VERSION 2 adds the second experiment mode, `experiment: wur` (Workspace Uptake & Retention), alongside the 7-rung context ladder. Every v2 key is optional and `model` is no longer required, so a v1 ladder job.yaml — including templates/job.example.yaml — validates unchanged. Cross-key semantics (a wur job needs conditions[] and facts_file; a ladder job needs environments[]) are NOT enforced here on purpose: jobspec.py mutates a spec key by key via `set`, re-validating after each write, so a schema that demanded a complete wur spec would reject every intermediate state. Those checks belong in jobspec._semantic_checks().

allOf.description: A job needs work to do: either a `tasks` list, or the single-task shorthand `task` + `accept`. IMPLEMENTATION.md §8.1 specified this as an if/then; it was left as an unconditional `required: [task, accept]`, so multi-task specs only validated because jobspec._normalize_tasks mirrored task 1 back to the top level. With that mirror correctly removed for multi-task jobs, this clause is what keeps them valid.

condition_id.description: A WUR arm id. Free-form by design, not an enum: §7.1 names 12 arms (d0-push, d1-ptr, d1, d2, d3, d2-check, d2-table, d2-dist, ctrl, ctrl-nofile, d1-np, d3-np) and the §7.2 pilot already adds a 13th (ctrl-np), so a closed list here would have to be edited before the pilot could run.

schema_version.description: "1" = ladder-only spec. "2" = may carry the wur keys below.

model.description: DEPRECATED in v2 — superseded by agent{backend, model, effort}, which separates the resolver key from the concrete model id. Kept as a free string (the v1 enum is gone) so existing job.yaml files keep working and so a new model id does not require a schema edit. jobspec._model_of(spec) is the one reader: it prefers agent.model, then agent.backend, then this.

agent.description: v2. Two-level model selection: `backend` picks the CLI adapter, `model` the concrete id it is invoked with, `effort` the backend-specific reasoning knob (null where the backend has none).

model.description: e.g. claude-sonnet-5. Null = the backend's own default.

reps.description: Runs per (task, condition) cell. Reps sample decoding noise, not population — task is the unit of generalization.

environments.description: Ladder mode only: the 7-rung context ladder.

experiment.description: v2. Which instrument to run. `ladder` is the existing context-ladder job and is the default when absent, so nothing that works today changes. `wur` skips context_gen.py entirely and runs the fact / plant / leak-check / canary / gate / schedule chain instead.

conditions.description: v2, wur mode: the arms to run, replacing `environments`. §7.1's 12 arms hold filename constant (NOTES.md at every depth) so filename salience is never confounded with depth.

baseline_condition.description: v2. The arm every other arm is differenced against: "E0" in ladder mode, "ctrl" in wur mode (use is ALWAYS reported as lift over the paired control; raw rates appear only in the appendix). figures.py must thread this instead of hard-coding env == "E0", which yields 0.00x for every arm but one under a label reading "normalized to E0 = 1.00".

facts_file.description: v2, wur mode: path to the fact registry (facts.yaml). Minted nonces, detector bindings, and the tier-(b) paraphrase regexes that must be FROZEN BEFORE ANY DATA. The live copy lives at $JOB_DIR/.registry/facts.yaml, mode 700, and must never be reachable from a workspace (V9).

tier.description: v2. D6: v1 runs Tier A (the synthetic fixture) only; Tier B (generated facts on arbitrary repos) is a follow-on job. Recorded on every row so the two pool later.

pointer_regime.description: v2. Job-level default for how an arm that carries a pointer renders it: none | prose (a prose pointer in CLAUDE.md) | import (an @NOTES.md import stub, which is simultaneously a push mechanism AND the strongest possible pointer — the confound d1-ptr exists to split).

matrix_seed.description: v2. Seed for the blocked randomisation frozen into schedule.json. NOT the probe cadence seed: cadence.schedule() is seeded by (salt, task_id, rep) only, deliberately not by arm, so every arm of a (task, rep) fires its k-th probe at the same barrier index and probe timing becomes a matched covariate.

probe.description: v2, wur mode: the probe subsystem's knobs. Defaults are the §6.2 values. The frozen TEXT is not configurable — it lives in lib/wur/protocol.py and is sha256-stamped into run_meta.json.

enabled.description: False for the no-probe arms (d1-np, d3-np), which bound probe reactivity. Per-arm override; this is the job-level default.

lo.description: Cadence interval lower bound, in tool calls.

max_probes.description: Cost bound: unbounded ~U{1,2,3} intervals over the step budget imply ~60 probes/run at ~350 output tokens each, ~20k tokens of pure instrument.

salt.description: Cadence seed salt. Changing it re-randomizes every future run relative to every past one.

max_retries.description: RETRY_TEXT re-asks per probe when the answer does not parse.

max_resumes.description: Consecutive RESUME_TEXT injections on a zero-tool-call result. Sent IDENTICALLY in the no-probe arms, so it is not a probed-arm-only intervention.

gate_timeout_ms.description: Barrier poll timeout. On expiry the hook prints {} and FAILS OPEN — a harness failure must never wedge a run.

budget.description: v2. Per-run stop conditions. There is no --max-turns in Claude Code 2.1.222, and deny-with-reason does not stop a run (the model treats the deny reason as injection and re-issues the same call, which then succeeds, V14) — so `steps` is enforced as deny-every-subsequent-call PLUS closing stdin.

steps.description: Step budget in tool calls; also the `budget` argument to cadence.schedule(). MEASURED FLOOR: at steps=8 every agent in the smoke matrix spent the entire budget orienting and never opened the planted file, so read/used/retained were structurally zero and the instrument measured nothing. Do not go below ~30 without re-checking read_rate(d1) against pilot gate G2.

max_usd.description: Passed as --max-budget-usd. Under a Max subscription there is no per-token bill, so this is an API-equivalent opportunity cost.

parallelism.description: v2. Sliding-window concurrency. JOBS <= 4 is verified against a real repo (S3: four worktrees, four isolated CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIRs, all clean); 6 is the untested ceiling. Parallelism is only safe because per-run CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR + --settings replaced the global ~/.claude/settings.json mutation.

per_backend.description: Backend policy table replacing the hard JOBS=1 clamp. A backend absent here inherits `jobs`.

discovery_regime.description: v2, wur mode. IMPLEMENTATION.md §7.1: whether ANY file in the workspace names the planted file. 'discovery' = nothing points at NOTES.md, so read-rate measures SEARCH. 'routing' = a byte-identical README.md in every arm carries one path line that varies, so read-rate measures whether the agent FOLLOWS a pointer. These are different experiments and are not comparable within one model, so this is a BETWEEN-job factor. Distinct from `pointer_regime`, which is the per-arm CLAUDE.md render mechanism (none|prose|import); the two were conflated under one name in the first cut, which left the §7.1 requirement that this be 'a declared knob, not an accident' unmet.
